title: Carbon dioxide removal MRV standards
bottleneck: Every CDR method — DAC, biochar, weathering, soils, oceans — needs its own measurement, reporting, and verification protocol, yet standards are fragmented across registries with inconsistent definitions of net removal, permanence, and leakage. Buyers cannot compare a tonne from one method to a tonne from another, and weak standards let low-quality credits undercut rigorous ones. No single authority sets the rules.
why_it_blocks: Without trusted MRV, the carbon removal market cannot scale: corporate buyers fear reputational risk and regulators cannot count removals toward national targets. The standards gap is now a bigger constraint on CDR than the underlying technology for several methods.
current_state: The EU's carbon removal certification framework and ISO efforts are pushing toward harmonization, and independent rating agencies now score credit quality. But a unified, science-based MRV regime accepted across markets is still years away.
